decisions.scenario: Finding an evening train from Cambridge to London Liverpool Street and checking the fare

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I'm looking for a train from Cambridge to London Liverpool Street.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: I can help with that. What day will you be travelling?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Tuesday, leaving sometime after 19:45.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Train TR3515 leaves Cambridge at 19:59 on Tuesday and arrives at London Liverpool Street at 21:27. Would you like me to book it?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Not yet. Could you please tell me the price?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: The fare is 16.60 pounds. Would you like to reserve any tickets?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: No, thank you. That's all I need.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: All right. If you decide to reserve tickets later, we would be happy to help.

decisions.notes: Normalized the incomplete booking exchange conservatively: the source never supplies passenger count or a booking reference and the closing turn indicates no reservation was completed, so the dialogue is framed as a fare enquiry without inventing a booking.
